featured_reviews.name: Danish Mehta
featured_reviews.review_text:
Toooo Goooddd!!! This place offers so many cuisines that your mind will be confused right from the start. It includes everything from indian and sindhi to mexican, italian and arabic; also offers asian and exotic food items such as fondues. Has a seating area on entry and on the first floor too. Coming to my experience here, it was a mixed review since we had problems related to the air-conditioner and it's management. We sat on the first floor and there's a staircase to reach there. Ambience at both the levels is great and superb!! While the ambience was great, the air-conditioner was equally unrewarding since they weren't working properly. We even reported that to the staff but they said that they already know it's not working and started pretending that they've called the technicians at 4 in the evening the same day!! So even after coming through such scorching heat outside, the inside wasn't much different. Finally after shifting places thrice, we found a spot where cool air could be felt! Apart from all this the food was sooo yummy, fresh and adequate in quantity that my brain didn't have any other issue to focus on!🙌
Food review-
1.Cream of Tomato with Basil soup- 5/5 for quantity, 5/5 for taste. Also they serve extra croutons if asked for!!🤭
2. Pahadi paneer tikka- 5/5 for quantity, 5/5 for taste. The paneer pieces were soooo soft and felt really fresh!!
3. Lasagne Ala Napolitano- 3/5 for quantity, 4/5 for taste. Was less in quantity as compared to other places i've had lasagne. Less cheesy as per the standard flavour of lasagne.
4. Dum aloo punjabi- 10/5 for quantity, 10/5 for taste. Reallly reallly very goood in everythinggg from quantity to taste to the dum aloo pieces. Usually 1 potato is provided but here 2 were provided and it's masala and gravy was also soo yummm!!!😋
5. Butter kulcha- 5/5 for taste. Soft, fresshhhh and buttery!!
6. Chinese sizzler- 1/5 for quantity and 1/5 for taste. Typically a chinese sizzler consists of rice, noodles, manchurian balls, chinese gravy and sautéd veggies. But this consisted just of rice, noodles and sautéd veggies. There were no manchurian balls nor there was any gravy which adds to the taste in sizzlers. REALLY A BIG WASTE OF MONEY, I WOULDN'T RECOMMEND YOU TO ORDER ANY SIZZLER AFTER TRYING THIS ONE AS THIS WAS OVERPRICED AS COMPARED TO ANY OTHER PLACE.
7. Basil Citrus Breeze Margarita- 5/5 for look, 3/5 for taste. Looks too fancy and delicious but is just okay. Full of ice and  essence. Won't matter if you don't try this.

featured_reviews.name: Koustubh Athavale
featured_reviews.review_text:
First off - it’s quite expensive, so I’m not factoring that into this review.

The food is new and comforting at the same time, like a vintage car with a brand new engine. The drinks are thought out and the cocktails might actually deserve their four-digit price tags. Have a chat with the bartender and he’ll explain where the liquor comes from, how long the flavor has to sit in a dungeon before being released, and maybe give you a taster if you’re nice enough.

Imagery aside:

- the food tastes great;
- the portions are surprisingly large for similar restaurants in Mumbai (which does make up for the price somewhat);
- the drinks are memorable (unless you have too many); and
- the ambience is fine - it’s on a busy Bandra street though so I think they’ve done well with what they had. You can still see Salt Water Café’s bones sticking through the walls (the place that was here before Bandra Born was…born)

All in all - I would and have and will recommend this place to my friends and family.

Some photos attached and specific recommendations below:

1. Granny’s prawn dish - raw mango bits, soft buns, CURRY 11/10
2. Malai podi toast - 9/10 (but refreshing)
3. Raviraj at the bar recommends and serves great drinks

Don't expect full-fledged restaurant type service or *perfectly* spiced potatoes - this one knows its audience and caters to it well. They've got bacon quiches, shephards pie, boat-type flatbreads, pattices, rolls, cutlets, and the usual snacks that will keep you coming back. I even do them with my favourite marmalade as a breakfast snack sometimes.

They also have heavier meal options like the cafreal roast with mash/veggies, stuffed meat poies with wedges, and filling burgers. The foods not always a 100% authentic, but usually quite satisfying. I've never tried their biryanis and rice dishes but those are available too. Everything is also quite reasonably priced for a premium bandra location.

Thanks for serving, family style 🤘. Reminds me of simpler times when getting a good meal didn't require you to shell out big money.

First off—the Whoppers. This is where this branch really shines. The flame-grilled taste hits different, with that smoky flavour Burger King is known for worldwide  . The burgers here often come out fresh, stacked properly, and tasting like an actual proper feed—not rushed or sloppy. Whether it’s a classic Whopper or a double, it’s got that juicy bite that makes you think, “yeah, this is why I came.”

The menu itself is packed with all the usual favourites—burgers, fries, sides, desserts—so you’re never short of options  . And when everything’s done right, it honestly feels like one of the best-tasting Burger King meals you can get anywhere in Auckland.

Now let’s talk about the real bonus: those bundle deals. Pulling up and getting a full combo plus something like a Baby Yoda (Grogu) mug? That’s elite. It’s not just food at that point—it’s an experience. You’re leaving with a full stomach and something cool to keep, which lowkey makes it feel way more worth it.

Service can be a bit hit-or-miss sometimes (like most fast food spots), but when they’re on point, the place runs smooth and delivers exactly what you want—quick, hot, and tasty food  .

Final take:
If you catch this spot on a good day, it genuinely feels like the best Burger King in Auckland. The Whoppers slap, the bundles are worth it, and the overall vibe hits when you’re hungry. Definitely one of those places that keeps you coming back.

🍔 Burgers:

#Daebak Fried Chicken Burger – 3.5/5
Good, spicy, and Korean-style, but slightly too oily for my taste. The Korean sauces were a bit overpowering, which dulled the overall flavour. Still decent if you like bold, saucy burgers.

#Chicken Smash Hit Burger – 5/5
Absolutely loved this one! Small, juicy, and super tasty. This was my first chicken smash burger, and it was cooked perfectly with great flavour.

#Veg Jaw Breaker (Double Patty) – 4.5/5
The name says it all! Huge burger and definitely difficult to eat in one bite 😄
It’s the costliest veg option but worth it stuffed with paneer, patties, and veggies. Very filling and tasty.

🧀 Starters:

Mozzarella Cheese Sticks – 4.5/5
Crispy on the outside, gooey on the inside. Pure cheese taste and fried really well.

🍟 Sides & Drinks:

Peri Peri Fries & Mojito – 4.5/5
Both were really good and complemented the burgers nicely.

⏰ Crowd & Location:

We went on a Saturday evening, so it was quite crowded. Had to wait around 20 minutes for seating.

Reaching Bandra itself can take time on weekends. Parking info isn’t clear we came by auto.

📍 Other Outlets:
They also have outlets in Thane, Vashi, Malad, and Andheri.

Overall: Great food, especially the chicken burgers. Slight wait time on weekends, but totally worth it for burger lovers 🍔🔥

I hae been a regular at EAC since 2019. It has been my go-to for years, and while it remains a staple in my Bandra circuit, have noticed some shifts lately that are hard to ignore.
The freshness of their ingredients is honestly amazing - you can taste the quality in every bite. Over the years, I have tried almost everything on the menu across all sections, except for their new bread menu and the salads.
​The Food Journey
​When it comes to the food, I have had nearly all their desserts. If they have the Opera Pastry, it is a absolute must-try. On the other hand, the Tiramisu was just average. If you're going for a drink, the Pineapple Coriander Cooler and the Spiced Mojito are my absolute favorites, but the Vietnamese Cold Coffee is extremely bad - a hard skip.
For mains, their Chicken Burgers, especially the Peri Peri and Grilled Chicken, are top-notch. The Paneer Roasted Veggie Sandwich is also amazing. If you are there for breakfast, the Eggs Benedict is definitely the highlight.
​Pro Tip: You have to try their Roast Chicken with Mashed Potatoes; it is easily their most famous and iconic dish. Hard skip - anything fish.
However, lately, I have noticed the quality seems to have taken a dip. It is not a massive drop, but they have been increasing their SKUs (adding more items), and it is hard not to notice that the consistency isn't what it used to be.
The seating layout here is easily the best of any cafe in Bandra, but a recent experience with the crowd has made me think about stopping my visits completely.
​We were sitting near a table that was loud - uncomfortably loud. A man accompanied by two ladies spent hours shouting. It started with "India vs. Pakistan" and how "we will decimate them," then moved to "India vs. USA" and how the USA is so much better. It turned ugly when he started shitting on Hinduism, calling it a "pagan religion" and preaching Christianity. He kept saying India is "poor, filthy, and bad" because of Hindus and that people should go to churches to "get civilized."
It was highly uncomfortable and left us feeling genuinely shook. I took three weeks to think about whether I should even post this, but the experience was that bad.

Time to hunt for a new go to place.

EATC is meant to be a welcoming, respectful space for everyone, and we regret that you felt uncomfortable. This is not the atmosphere we strive to create, and we will be reinforcing this with our team.

Regards,
EATC Team.

featured_reviews.name: Riddhiman Chanda
featured_reviews.review_text:
Linking Road in Bandra is home to some of the best food in the city, and one of the best asian joints in the place is The fatty Bao. It has a modern, chic vibe crossed with a vibrant and sassy decor, perfect for a date night, or for a hangout sesh with friends.

The decor feels inspired by Malay/Singaporean cafes, with a lot of the artwork depicting the same, and it comes off pretty well. They have both indoor and outdoor seating, though the indoor seating is a bit cramped, but that's mostly fine. They do have a small bar serving the usual suspects, as well as some of their own stuff.

While I didn't get to order a large chunk of their menu, whatever I had was pretty great. Their name is definitely apt, as the baos I got were plump and pillowy, and the filling was perfect. I got the pork char siu baos, and the pork was fatty and melt in your mouth, complimented nicely by a slice of raw apple, giving it a fruity kick. Every Bao order comes with two, making it perfect for date night.

I also got their raw papaya salad, which was one of the best renditions of the dish I've eaten in Mumbai. It was tangy, sweet and spicy in just the right amounts, and wasn't just a refreshing palate cleanser, but a great meal by itself. It's also a very generous portion making it great for sharing.

The last thing I got were Chicken and asparagus dumplings, which didn't impress me as much, as I've had better dumplings in the same price range. They weren't bad but not particularly great either. The filling was generous, but it lacked in flavor. For 6 pieces, it was not the best value, and I recommend trying other dumplings, or avoiding dumplings all together.

Overall, I would rate both the Char Siu Bao and the Papaya Salad a solid 9/10, and the dumplings about a 6.5/10. Definitely go for their baos( pretty obvious given their name).

The service was fine, but they do tend to ignore the smaller tables and focus on the bigger groups, and it was also pretty busy on the day I visited. But I did see other tables also not receiving food at the proper times, so I'd rate the service a little lower, like a 6/10. Definitely could do with some improvement.

The Fatty Bao definitely ticks a lot of the boxes, though they do miss a little bit in their service, and cocktail variety, though I did not have the opportunity to try it. However, they more than make up for it with their snazzy decor and contemporary vibe, along with some pretty great food. I highly recommend checking the place out if you're out shopping in Linking Road and need to grab some lunch or dinner. You're definitely gonna be leaving a happy and fatty bao when you're done.

Final rating- 8.5/10, definitely recommend.
